answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The basalt report makes public the merge explicitly at each timber. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 46 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 286 times the capital for one share. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
